title: Supreme Court Temporarily Restores Access to Abortion Pill by Mail
partialText: A lower-court ruling had reinstated a Food and Drug Administration requirement that patients visit a health care provider in person to obtain mifepristone.

title: Oil Jumps as Iran Resists Trump’s Offer to Help Ships Through Strait of Hormuz
partialText: Oil prices fell and futures on the S&P 500 rose slightly on Sunday as investors reacted to continued uncertainty about the war in Iran.

title: China Seeks an Advantage With Both Trump and Iran as War Evolves
partialText: With President Trump’s visit to Beijing looming, China is pushing Iran to negotiate even as its companies export material that could be used by Iran’s military.

title: Confusion in Strait of Hormuz Leaves Shipping Firms Guessing
partialText: The United States vowed to help tankers navigate the perilous conditions that have kept them stranded in the Persian Gulf, but it remained unclear if companies would try to get out.

title: The U.S. Army’s ‘Big Experiment’ in the Arctic Cold
partialText: How would soldiers from places like Florida, Texas and Georgia fight and persevere in temperatures as low as minus 40 degrees?

title: Trump Backed Forced Treatment for Homeless People. Utah Shows the Challenges.
partialText: State lawmakers declined to back a Trump-inspired plan to move 1,300 homeless people to a campus on the edge of Salt Lake City, but supporters are trying to keep the plan’s spirit alive.

title: Rudy Giuliani Hospitalized in Florida in ‘Critical Condition’
partialText: A spokesman for the former mayor of New York City said Mr. Giuliani was now breathing on his own.

title: The Met Gala’s Embrace of Jeff Bezos Causes a Backlash
partialText: Protesters have found a perfect foil in Amazon’s founder, the gala’s lead sponsor this year.

partialText: A stalwart on defense spending, Poland is training its citizens in civil defense while balancing their jobs and families.

partialText: Top leaders believe losing 5,000 U.S. troops will not hurt German security. But analysts fear an economic hit, especially in military communities.

title: The Return for These Investors Isn’t Money, It’s More Affordable Housing
partialText: Local governments are trying to create housing that is permanently affordable by investing directly in construction. They are rewriting how housing programs have traditionally operated.

title: A 22,000-Home Community Is Being Built in a 5,000-Person Town
partialText: Chatham Park, a master-planned community in Pittsboro, N.C., is expected to expand the town to 60,000 people when completed.

title: Chasing Stardom in Korea Nearly Destroyed Ejae. Then Came ‘KPop Demon Hunters.’
partialText: Ejae, the movie’s breakout star, was the face of K-pop in 2025. Facing questions of art, national belonging and authenticity, she wants to be much more.

title: How the Kremlin Lures Africans Into Russia’s War in Ukraine
partialText: A growing number of men across the continent say they are being promised jobs in Russia, only to be forced into the war. Some go as mercenaries, but many more are drawn unwittingly.

title: Why Are Africans Fighting in Russia’s War in Ukraine?
partialText: Some see a clear explanation: Russia needs more troops, and young men in Africa desperately need jobs.

title: Drone Hits a Moscow High-Rise Days Before a Major Military Parade
partialText: Air defenses in the Russian capital were breached as Ukraine expands long-range strikes.

title: School Cellphone Ban Study Finds Mixed Results
partialText: Cellphone bans got devices out of students’ hands, according to the first large study. But behavior and academics have not improved, at least so far.

title: Democrats Add 8 Candidates to House Battlefield Program for Midterms
partialText: The party’s congressional campaign arm is promoting more contenders to take down at-risk Republicans — and is taking sides in some competitive primaries.

title: A Medical Examiner Chases Down an Elusive Killer
partialText: Unusual opioids are infiltrating street drugs. Knoxville’s top forensic doctor is on the front lines, pressing to quickly identify the most lethal.

title: What to Know About Orphines, a New Class of Deadly Opioids
partialText: The drugs are 10 times more dangerous than fentanyl. They are showing up in street drugs in the South and the Midwest, and will most likely spread to other regions.

title: Is Loving Food the Secret to Eating Less of It?
partialText: The case for ditching self-denial and embracing enjoyment.

title: What to Know About the Suspected Hantavirus Outbreak on an Atlantic Cruise Ship

partialText: Three people aboard a cruise ship sailing the Atlantic Ocean have died from what health officials suspect were hantavirus infections.

title: John Sterling, the Yankees’ Most Enduring Announcer, Dies at 87

partialText: Israel has failed to arrest a wave of violence against Palestinians, prompting military officials to urge the government to intervene.

partialText: The pop star was arrested in March after officers in California observed her driving erratically. She later checked herself into a treatment facility.

title: The ‘Gates to Hell’ Are Dimming. That May Not Be a Good Thing.
partialText: A flaming crater of gas has burned in Turkmenistan for decades. Satellite imagery suggests that the fires are decreasing, but the environmental implications are unclear.

title: A Strong El Niño May Be Coming. Global Warming Is Changing Its Effects.
partialText: As the planet warms, past episodes of the natural weather phenomenon may no longer be a reliable guide of how the next one plays out.
